title: Magellan's Expedition Sets Sail Around the World
shortDesc: Five ships leave Spain on the first voyage to circle the globe.
fullDesc: In September 1519 Ferdinand Magellan led five ships from Spain to find a western route to the Spice Islands. Magellan died in the Philippines in 1521, and one ship under Juan Sebastián Elcano completed the first circumnavigation in 1522.
realFacts: Only 18 of about 240 men returned
Magellan found the strait that now bears his name
The voyage proved how large the Pacific is
Spain gained a claim to Pacific trade

title: Cortés Conquers the Aztec Capital
shortDesc: Tenochtitlan falls and the Aztec Empire collapses.
fullDesc: In August 1521 Hernán Cortés and his Spanish forces, with thousands of Indigenous allies, took the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan after a long siege. Disease, especially smallpox, devastated the city's defenders.
realFacts: Mexico City was built on the ruins
Smallpox killed a large share of the population
Indigenous allies such as the Tlaxcalans were crucial
New Spain was ruled for about 300 years

title: Pizarro Captures the Inca Emperor
shortDesc: A small Spanish force seizes Atahualpa and topples the Inca Empire.
fullDesc: In November 1532 Francisco Pizarro and about 170 Spaniards captured the Inca emperor Atahualpa at Cajamarca. Despite a huge ransom the emperor was executed, and the Spanish soon took control of the empire.
realFacts: The Inca were weakened by a civil war and disease
The ransom filled a room with gold and silver
Cusco fell in 1533
Resistance continued for decades
wiki: Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire

title: Henry VIII Breaks with Rome
shortDesc: The Act of Supremacy makes the king head of the Church of England.
fullDesc: In 1534 Parliament passed the Act of Supremacy, naming Henry VIII supreme head of the Church of England. The break began when the pope refused to annul his marriage to Catherine of Aragon.
realFacts: Henry dissolved the monasteries from 1536
He married six times
The church's doctrine shifted back and forth under his children
Thomas More was executed for refusing the oath

title: Copernicus Puts the Sun at the Centre
shortDesc: A book argues that the Earth orbits the Sun.
fullDesc: In 1543 Nicolaus Copernicus published De revolutionibus orbium coelestium, proposing that the Earth and other planets orbit the Sun. It began a long revolution in astronomy.
realFacts: He reportedly received a printed copy on his deathbed
Galileo and Kepler later supported the idea
The Church banned the book in 1616
It challenged the Earth-centred view from antiquity

title: The Battle of Lepanto
shortDesc: A Christian fleet defeats the Ottoman navy in the Mediterranean.
fullDesc: On October 7, 1571 a fleet of the Holy League, led by Spain and Venice, defeated the Ottoman navy at Lepanto off Greece. It was one of the largest galley battles in history.
realFacts: Miguel de Cervantes was wounded in the fight
The Ottomans rebuilt their fleet within a year
It was among the last major galley battles
It halted Ottoman naval expansion for a time

title: The Spanish Armada Is Defeated
shortDesc: England turns back a giant invasion fleet.
fullDesc: In 1588 Spain sent a fleet of about 130 ships to invade England. English ships, fire ships and bad weather scattered the Armada, and many vessels were wrecked on the long voyage home.
realFacts: Queen Elizabeth I gave a famous speech at Tilbury
Dozens of Spanish ships were lost
Spain remained a power for decades
England's confidence as a sea power grew

title: The East India Company Is Founded
shortDesc: A trading company that would come to rule much of India begins.
fullDesc: On December 31, 1600 Queen Elizabeth I granted a royal charter to the English East India Company to trade with Asia. Over time it grew into a private ruler of large parts of India.
realFacts: It had its own army and navy
It controlled much of India by the 1800s
The British government took over after the 1857 rebellion
The company was dissolved in 1874

title: Jamestown Is Founded
shortDesc: The first lasting English settlement in North America begins in Virginia.
fullDesc: In May 1607 about 100 English settlers founded Jamestown in Virginia. The colony nearly failed in its early years, but tobacco farming made it profitable.
realFacts: The winter of 1609 to 1610 is called the Starving Time
The first enslaved Africans arrived nearby in 1619
Pocahontas helped link the settlers and the Powhatan
Virginia became a royal colony in 1624

title: Galileo Turns a Telescope to the Sky
shortDesc: He sees moons around Jupiter and mountains on the Moon.
fullDesc: In 1609 and 1610 Galileo Galilei used a telescope he built to observe the heavens. He saw Jupiter's four largest moons, the Moon's craters and the phases of Venus, and published his findings in Sidereus Nuncius.
realFacts: The moons showed that not everything circled the Earth
The Church tried him in 1633 for supporting Copernicus
He spent his last years under house arrest
The Church admitted its error in 1992

title: The Mayflower Reaches New England
shortDesc: Pilgrims land at Plymouth and sign the Mayflower Compact.
fullDesc: In November 1620 the ship Mayflower reached Cape Cod with about 100 English passengers, many of them religious Separatists. Before landing they signed the Mayflower Compact and settled at Plymouth.
realFacts: About half died the first winter
The Wampanoag helped them survive
A harvest feast in 1621 is the basis of the Thanksgiving story
Plymouth remained a small colony

title: The Peace of Westphalia
shortDesc: Treaties end the Thirty Years' War and shape modern states.
fullDesc: The Peace of Westphalia in 1648 ended the Thirty Years' War, one of Europe's most destructive conflicts. It recognised the independence of states and is often seen as the origin of modern ideas of sovereignty.
realFacts: Millions died in the war from fighting, hunger and disease
The Dutch Republic's independence was confirmed
The Holy Roman Empire grew weaker
France and Sweden gained territory

title: King Charles I Is Executed
shortDesc: England puts its own king on trial and beheads him.
fullDesc: On January 30, 1649 King Charles I was beheaded in London after losing the English Civil War. England became a republic led by Oliver Cromwell.
realFacts: The monarchy was restored in 1660
Cromwell later became Lord Protector
It showed that a king could be held to account
The war killed a large share of the population

title: Newton Publishes the Principia
shortDesc: The laws of motion and gravity are set out in one book.
fullDesc: In 1687 Isaac Newton published Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica. It laid out his three laws of motion and the law of universal gravitation, which explained both falling apples and the orbits of planets.
realFacts: Edmond Halley encouraged and paid for its printing
It dominated physics for over 200 years
Einstein's relativity later refined it
Newton also developed calculus

title: The Glorious Revolution
shortDesc: William of Orange takes the English throne and Parliament gains power.
fullDesc: In 1688 William of Orange landed in England and James II fled, ending the Stuart king's rule with almost no fighting. A Bill of Rights in 1689 set limits on royal power.
realFacts: William and Mary ruled jointly
Parliament's power over taxes was secured
It influenced the American founders
Catholics were barred from the throne

title: Peter the Great Founds St. Petersburg
shortDesc: A new capital rises from the marshes as Russia looks west.
fullDesc: In 1703 Tsar Peter the Great founded St. Petersburg on swampy land by the Baltic Sea. It became Russia's capital and a symbol of his drive to modernise the country along European lines.
realFacts: Thousands of workers died building it
It was the capital until 1918
It was renamed Petrograd and then Leningrad
It took back the name St. Petersburg in 1991

title: The Lisbon Earthquake
shortDesc: A quake, tsunami and fire destroy one of Europe's great cities.
fullDesc: On November 1, 1755, All Saints' Day, a powerful earthquake struck Lisbon, followed by a tsunami and fires. Tens of thousands died, and the city was largely destroyed.
realFacts: The Marquis of Pombal led the rebuilding
It shook religious and philosophical beliefs in Europe
Voltaire wrote about it in Candide
It helped found the science of seismology

title: The American Revolutionary War Begins
shortDesc: Shots at Lexington and Concord start the fight for independence.
fullDesc: On April 19, 1775 British soldiers and colonial militia clashed at Lexington and Concord in Massachusetts. The fighting began the American Revolutionary War, often remembered as the shot heard round the world.
realFacts: Paul Revere and others rode to warn of the British march
The Declaration of Independence followed in 1776
France joined the American side in 1778
The war ended with the Treaty of Paris in 1783

title: The Siege of Yorktown
shortDesc: A British army surrenders and the American Revolution is effectively won.
fullDesc: In October 1781 General Cornwallis surrendered about 8,000 British troops at Yorktown, Virginia, after American and French forces trapped them by land and sea. It was the last major battle of the American Revolution.
realFacts: French ships blocked the British retreat
George Washington and Rochambeau led the allied armies
Peace talks began soon after
Britain recognised American independence in 1783

title: The First Hot Air Balloon Flights
shortDesc: The Montgolfier brothers lift people into the sky for the first time.
fullDesc: In 1783 Joseph and Étienne Montgolfier flew hot air balloons in France. In November two men, Pilâtre de Rozier and the Marquis d'Arlandes, made the first free flight carrying humans over Paris.
realFacts: An earlier test carried a sheep, a duck and a rooster
The flight crossed about 9 km of Paris
Hydrogen balloons soon followed
It started the age of aviation

title: The Haitian Revolution Begins
shortDesc: Enslaved people in Saint-Domingue rise up and found a free nation.
fullDesc: In August 1791 enslaved people in the French colony of Saint-Domingue began a revolt that grew into a full revolution. Under leaders such as Toussaint Louverture, it ended slavery and led to Haiti's independence in 1804.
realFacts: Haiti became the first Black republic
Toussaint Louverture died in a French prison in 1803
Jean-Jacques Dessalines declared independence in 1804
France later demanded a huge payment from Haiti

title: Louis XVI Is Guillotined
shortDesc: The French king is executed and the Terror begins.
fullDesc: On January 21, 1793 King Louis XVI was executed by guillotine in Paris after being convicted of treason. The revolution then entered its radical phase, the Reign of Terror.
realFacts: Marie Antoinette was executed that October
Robespierre led the Committee of Public Safety
Tens of thousands died in the Terror
Robespierre himself was guillotined in 1794

title: The Rosetta Stone Is Found
shortDesc: A slab with three scripts becomes the key to Egyptian hieroglyphs.
fullDesc: In 1799 French soldiers in Egypt found the Rosetta Stone, carved with the same text in hieroglyphs, Demotic and Greek. In 1822 Jean-François Champollion used it to decipher hieroglyphs.
realFacts: The British captured it from the French in 1801
It has been in the British Museum since 1802
It dates to 196 BC
Egypt has asked for its return

title: The Louisiana Purchase
shortDesc: The United States doubles in size by buying land from France.
fullDesc: In 1803 the United States bought the Louisiana Territory from France for about 15 million dollars. The purchase roughly doubled the size of the country.
realFacts: Napoleon sold it partly to fund his wars
Lewis and Clark explored it from 1804
It included land for 15 future states
It allowed westward expansion to accelerate

title: The Battle of Trafalgar
shortDesc: Nelson wins a decisive naval victory but dies in the fight.
fullDesc: On October 21, 1805 a British fleet under Admiral Horatio Nelson defeated the combined French and Spanish fleets off Cape Trafalgar. Nelson was killed in the battle, but Britain secured its naval dominance.
realFacts: Napoleon gave up plans to invade Britain
Nelson's flagship was HMS Victory
Britain ruled the seas for a century
Nelson's Column stands in London

title: The Eruption of Mount Tambora
shortDesc: The largest volcanic eruption in recorded history causes a year without a summer.
fullDesc: In April 1815 Mount Tambora in Indonesia erupted in the most powerful volcanic eruption in recorded history. Ash and gas cooled the planet, and 1816 became known as the year without a summer.
realFacts: Tens of thousands died directly
Crops failed in Europe and North America
It may have inspired Mary Shelley's Frankenstein
Global temperatures dropped by about 0.4 to 0.7 degrees

title: The First Public Steam Railway Opens
shortDesc: A locomotive hauls passengers and coal in northern England.
fullDesc: On September 27, 1825 the Stockton and Darlington Railway opened in England, with George Stephenson's locomotive pulling the first train. It was the first public railway to use steam locomotives.
realFacts: The Liverpool and Manchester Railway followed in 1830
Stephenson's Rocket won the Rainhill Trials in 1829
Railways spread rapidly across the world
Travel times fell dramatically

title: The First Opium War Begins
shortDesc: Britain fights China over trade and the opium that flowed into the country.
fullDesc: In 1839 China moved to stop the British opium trade, and war followed. Britain's navy won, and the Treaty of Nanking in 1842 gave Britain Hong Kong and opened Chinese ports to trade.
realFacts: Hong Kong stayed British until 1997
A second Opium War began in 1856
China later called this a century of humiliation
Opium addiction was widespread in China

title: Morse Sends the First Telegraph Message
shortDesc: What hath God wrought travels by wire from Washington to Baltimore.
fullDesc: On May 24, 1844 Samuel Morse sent the message What hath God wrought from Washington to Baltimore over an electric telegraph line. Messages could now travel faster than any rider.
realFacts: Morse code was developed with Alfred Vail
A transatlantic cable was laid in 1858
The telegraph linked continents within decades
It changed news and business

title: The California Gold Rush
shortDesc: Gold found at Sutter's Mill sets off a stampede west.
fullDesc: In January 1848 James Marshall found gold at Sutter's Mill in California. News spread in 1848 and 1849, and about 300,000 people came, changing California forever.
realFacts: San Francisco grew from a village to a city
California became a state in 1850
Indigenous people suffered greatly
Levi Strauss later made his name selling jeans to miners

title: The Communist Manifesto and the Revolutions of 1848
shortDesc: Marx and Engels publish as uprisings sweep Europe.
fullDesc: In February 1848 Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels published The Communist Manifesto. That year revolutions broke out across Europe, though most were put down within a year.
realFacts: Revolts began in France and spread to Germany, Italy and Austria
Most failed in the short term
The manifesto became hugely influential later
Marx spent much of his life in London

title: Commodore Perry Opens Japan
shortDesc: American warships force Japan to end its isolation.
fullDesc: In July 1853 US Navy Commodore Matthew Perry sailed warships into Edo Bay and demanded that Japan open to trade. The treaty signed in 1854 ended more than 200 years of near isolation.
realFacts: The shogunate's weakness was exposed
It helped lead to the Meiji Restoration in 1868
Japan modernised rapidly afterwards
The Black Ships became a symbol of the opening

title: The Indian Rebellion of 1857
shortDesc: A revolt against the East India Company shakes British rule.
fullDesc: In 1857 Indian soldiers in the East India Company's army rose in revolt, and civilians joined them across northern India. It was crushed, and in 1858 the British Crown took direct control of India.
realFacts: It began at Meerut in May 1857
Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi became a symbol of resistance
The last Mughal emperor was exiled
The British Raj lasted until 1947

title: The American Civil War Begins at Fort Sumter
shortDesc: Confederate guns open fire on a Union fort in Charleston.
fullDesc: On April 12, 1861 Confederate forces fired on Fort Sumter in Charleston harbor, South Carolina. The attack began the American Civil War, which lasted four years.
realFacts: No one was killed in the bombardment itself
Lincoln called for 75,000 volunteers
About 620,000 soldiers died in the war
Four more states joined the Confederacy

title: The Battle of Gettysburg
shortDesc: The bloodiest battle of the Civil War turns the tide for the Union.
fullDesc: From July 1 to 3, 1863 Union and Confederate armies fought at Gettysburg, Pennsylvania, with some 50,000 casualties in three days. Robert E. Lee's army retreated, and Lincoln later gave the Gettysburg Address there.
realFacts: Pickett's Charge failed on the last day
Vicksburg fell to Grant the next day
Lincoln's speech was about 272 words
It was the largest battle in North America

title: Lee Surrenders at Appomattox
shortDesc: The main Confederate army gives up and the Civil War ends.
fullDesc: On April 9, 1865 General Robert E. Lee surrendered the Army of Northern Virginia to Ulysses S. Grant at Appomattox Court House. It effectively ended the American Civil War.
realFacts: Grant gave generous terms
Lincoln was assassinated five days later
Other Confederate armies surrendered over the next weeks
Reconstruction followed
wiki: Appomattox Court House National Historical Park

title: The Meiji Restoration
shortDesc: Japan restores imperial rule and modernises at speed.
fullDesc: In 1868 the Tokugawa shogunate ended and power returned to Emperor Meiji. Japan then rapidly industrialised and built a modern army, becoming a major power within a generation.
realFacts: The samurai class lost its privileges
Railways and a national army were built
Japan defeated China in 1895 and Russia in 1905
The capital moved to Tokyo

title: The Transcontinental Railroad Is Completed
shortDesc: A golden spike joins the American coasts by rail.
fullDesc: On May 10, 1869 the Central Pacific and Union Pacific railroads met at Promontory Summit, Utah, with a ceremonial golden spike. The trip across the country, which once took months, now took about a week.
realFacts: Thousands of Chinese workers built the Central Pacific line
Irish immigrants built much of the Union Pacific
It sped settlement of the West
It harmed the Plains Indians and the buffalo

title: Germany Is Unified
shortDesc: Bismarck's wars create a German Empire.
fullDesc: On January 18, 1871 the German Empire was proclaimed at the Palace of Versailles, after Prussia and its allies defeated France in the Franco-Prussian War. Otto von Bismarck had united the German states under Prussian leadership.
realFacts: Wilhelm I became emperor
France lost Alsace-Lorraine
Germany became Europe's strongest power
The resentment helped set the stage for World War I

title: The Great Chicago Fire
shortDesc: A fire burns for days and destroys much of the city.
fullDesc: On October 8, 1871 a fire broke out in Chicago and burned for about two days, destroying thousands of buildings. About 300 people died and 100,000 lost their homes.
realFacts: The cause is still uncertain
The legend of Mrs. O'Leary's cow is probably untrue
Chicago was rebuilt quickly
The city became a centre of new skyscraper design

title: Krakatoa Erupts
shortDesc: One of history's loudest explosions is heard thousands of kilometres away.
fullDesc: On August 27, 1883 the volcano Krakatoa in Indonesia exploded, creating tsunamis that killed more than 36,000 people. The sound was heard thousands of kilometres away, and the ash caused vivid sunsets around the world.
realFacts: Most deaths were caused by tsunamis
Global temperatures dipped for a few years
Telegraph lines helped spread the news worldwide
A new volcano, Anak Krakatau, later grew in the same spot

title: The Berlin Conference and the Scramble for Africa
shortDesc: European powers set rules for carving up Africa.
fullDesc: From 1884 to 1885 European powers met in Berlin to set rules for claiming territory in Africa. No African leaders took part, and within decades almost the whole continent was divided into colonies.
realFacts: Belgium's King Leopold II received the Congo
Borders ignored local peoples and cultures
Only Ethiopia and Liberia remained independent
Many modern borders date from this period

title: The Statue of Liberty Is Dedicated
shortDesc: A gift from France becomes a symbol of welcome in New York Harbor.
fullDesc: On October 28, 1886 the Statue of Liberty was dedicated on Liberty Island in New York. France gave the copper statue to the United States, and it became a symbol of freedom and welcome for immigrants.
realFacts: Frédéric Bartholdi designed it
Gustave Eiffel built the internal frame
Emma Lazarus's poem was added to its base in 1903
Millions of immigrants passed it on the way to Ellis Island

title: Jack the Ripper Terrorises London
shortDesc: Unsolved murders in Whitechapel make headlines around the world.
fullDesc: In the autumn of 1888 a series of murders of women in London's Whitechapel district were attributed to a killer nicknamed Jack the Ripper. He was never identified, and the case became a legend.
realFacts: At least five women are thought to be his victims
Press coverage was intense
Police received hundreds of letters, most hoaxes
It drew attention to poverty in the East End

title: The Eiffel Tower Opens
shortDesc: A giant iron tower becomes the symbol of Paris.
fullDesc: The Eiffel Tower opened in March 1889 as the entrance to the Paris World's Fair. At 300 metres it was the tallest structure in the world, and it was meant to stand for only 20 years.
realFacts: It was the world's tallest structure until 1930
Some artists protested its construction
It was saved partly by its use as a radio tower
Millions visit each year

title: The First Modern Olympic Games
shortDesc: Athens revives the ancient Games.
fullDesc: The first modern Olympic Games opened in Athens in April 1896, inspired by Pierre de Coubertin. About 240 male athletes from 14 nations competed.
realFacts: Spyridon Louis won the marathon for Greece
Women did not compete until 1900
The Games became truly global in the 20th century
The Winter Olympics began in 1924

title: Marie and Pierre Curie Discover Radium
shortDesc: Two new radioactive elements open the atomic age of science.
fullDesc: In 1898 Marie and Pierre Curie announced the discovery of two new radioactive elements, polonium and radium. Marie Curie won Nobel Prizes in 1903 in Physics and 1911 in Chemistry.
realFacts: She was the first person to win two Nobel Prizes
She remains the only one to win in two different sciences
She died in 1934 of an illness linked to radiation
Her work led to medical X-rays and cancer treatment

title: The Spanish-American War
shortDesc: A short war makes the United States an overseas power.
fullDesc: In 1898 the United States fought Spain over Cuba, after the battleship USS Maine exploded in Havana harbor. In a few months the US won and gained control of Puerto Rico, Guam and the Philippines.
realFacts: Cuba became nominally independent
The Philippine-American War followed
Theodore Roosevelt's Rough Riders became famous
The war marked America's emergence as a world power

title: The Boxer Rebellion
shortDesc: An uprising in China besieges the foreign legations in Beijing.
fullDesc: In 1900 the Boxers, a Chinese movement opposed to foreign influence, besieged the foreign legations in Beijing for 55 days. An eight-nation alliance relieved the city, and China was forced to pay heavy compensation.
realFacts: The Qing court backed the Boxers for a time
Thousands of Chinese Christians and foreigners were killed
The Boxer Protocol was signed in 1901
The Qing dynasty fell in 1911
